To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel multiple input multiple output convolution neural network ( MIMO-Net ) for cell segmentation in fluorescent microscopy images and our method outperformed the state of the art methods.
the proposed MIMO-Net is able to deal with variable size of cells, variable intensity boundaries, and variable intensity of the cells and outperforms the state-of-the-art methods for segmentation.
the proposed network is capable of learning multiple resolutions of the image simultaneously to improve the segmentation performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a novel multiple-input multi-output convolution neural network for cell detection and segmentation.
the problem of cell segmentation and classification in the context of pancreatic tissue.
the design of a deep learning based method for cell segmentation in microscopy images.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MIMO-Net outperforms state of the art deep learning approaches for the segmentation of cells in fluorescence microscopy images.
the MIMO-Net outperforms other deep learning methods for cell segmentation in terms of F1-score.
the proposed MIMO-Net is a powerful deep learning based approach for cell segmentation in the fluorescence microscopy images.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MIMO-Net is a novel multi-resolution network that is able to deal with variable cell size and variable cell intensity in microscopy images.
MIMO-Net is an effective deep learning based approach for segmenting nuclei in fluorescence microscopy images.
the proposed network is a robust method for segmenting cells from fluorescence microscopy images and can also be applied to other biomedical image analysis tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MIMO-Net can learn the features at different scales of the image to generate a segmentation mask.
the proposed network can handle the variable size cell segmentation in fluorescence images and can be used to segment cells in different microscopy images.
we can achieve better segmentation performance using a simple and computationally efficient MIMO-Net architecture.
